chunk_findings.detail: On Python 3.12+, f-string contents tokenize as `FSTRING_START`/`FSTRING_MIDDLE`/`FSTRING_END`, not as `tokenize.STRING`. The guard fails, even though no child process is started. Include the f-string token types in the protected set (or otherwise treat them as string regions).

chunk_findings.detail: The tab-column alignment the previous scanner relied on was removed, and the new comment is wrong for the interpreter this test still claims to support. On Python 3.11 `tokenize.generate_tokens` expands each tab to tabsize 8 when it records `(row, column)`, while `spawn.finditer` now runs on the raw line from `src.split("\n")`. Given `ddflow/foo.py` containing `x="\t";subprocess.run([])\n`, the STRING token’s expanded end column runs past the raw index of `subprocess` (string starts at raw column 2; the tab jumps the tokenizer to column 8, so the token ends at column 9, while `m.start()` is 6). The check `start <= (n, m.start()) < end` treats that real call as prose and `continue`s, so the unguarded spawn is never appended to `offenders` and the ratchet passes.

chunk_findings.detail:
By treating every match inside a `STRING` token as non-executable, the ratchet now misses a real unguarded spawn constructed as an evaluated string. For example, a file `ddflow/foo.py` containing
`import subprocess; exec("subprocess.run('echo hi')")`
has its `subprocess.run` occurrence inside a `STRING` token, so `any(start <= (n, m.start()) < end ...)` skips it and no offender is recorded. That module does spawn a child without going through `proc`, which is exactly the invariant this test exists to enforce; the old `spawn.search(line)` would have reported it.

    def test_every_guard_has_its_own_baseline_file_and_nothing_else_is_there() -> None:
        """One file per guard (a directory of files, one per module, for the PER_MODULE
        counters): each counter and each `.importlinter` contract has its baseline
        file, holding exactly its keys; `.importlinter` itself lists no allowlist (two homes
        for one list would drift); and no other file is there -- one left behind by a renamed
        or removed guard would be read by nothing while looking like it still guarded."""
